headline: Comparisons of biomolecular AI models expose thermodynamic and conformational determinants
label: Biomolecular Ai Model Evaluation
summary: Recent preprints and a published pKa study probe whether learned representations capture physical quantities, not only sequence patterns.
synthesis: The common thread is scrutiny of what learned biomolecular models encode and how sensitive their outputs are to method choice. A categorical Jacobian comparison of RNA-FM, Evo 2 and gLM2 finds that base-pair signals reflect thermodynamics, disentangling them from RNA evolution. Separately, a comparison of BioEmu, AFSample2 and ESMFlow shows that these ensemble predictors yield distinct conformational distributions, so their outputs call for cautious interpretation. In the pKa study, G-pKa couples a tautomer-compatible graph dataset of 6379 experimental values with 309 quantum chemical features, and benchmarks tree-ensemble and graph neural network predictors on that data. Taken together, the dominant focus is on feature-level interpretation and physical grounding rather than headline accuracy alone.
